summary: GRAMMER Aktiengesellschaft’s operating EBIT jumped to EUR 75.1 million in FY 2025 from EUR 41.6 million in FY 2024, yet an accumulated loss of EUR ‑244.1 million remains as of 31 Dec 2025 [6] [7] [8]. Net income swung to a EUR 17.2 million profit in FY 2025 from a EUR ‑115.2 million loss a year earlier, but no dividend is proposed because the loan agreement blocks payouts until 2027 [9] [10]. A U.S. class‑action alleges concealed defects in Active Head Restraints, and Grammer Inc. is suing APC Parent LLC for over $20 million withheld in a $40 million merger [11] [12]. report.headline: Americas logistics and tariff costs drive H1 2026 EBIT loss

findings.text: The Americas segment recorded an operating EBIT loss of EUR 6.2 million in H1 2026, explicitly attributed to additional logistics and tariff-related expenses, and flagged as a key risk for the second half of 2026.

Group management warned of a challenging market environment citing macroeconomic uncertainty, elevated material and energy costs, geopolitical developments, and potential disruptions from US tariff measures impacting global supply chains.
Americas revenue declined 7.7% to EUR 153.0 million in H1 2026 due to weaker demand and currency headwinds, indicating the region is shrinking while also losing money.

Despite the Americas loss, group operating EBIT rose 17.1% to EUR 41.7 million in H1 2026, driven by strong Q2 performance, efficiency initiatives under the 'Top 10' programme, and group-wide capacity adjustments.
The company completed long-term refinancing facilities of approximately EUR 762 million in H1 2026, enhancing financial clarity and providing liquidity headroom to absorb operational shocks.

Full-year 2026 guidance is maintained at around EUR 1.9 billion revenue and operating EBIT near EUR 80 million, implying management expects the Americas logistics and tariff drag to be contained or offset in H2.
